Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a short deck and a sample term worksheet with three options. High level summary here so procurement can pick what fits best: 

Option A — 1yr annual prepay (no prefund buffer)- Standard 12% discount off list for 1yr full prepay- Monthly usage true-up, credit applied in next invoice cycle- 30-day on/off exit cap (limited to 25% of committed ARR)

Option B — 1yr prepay + prefund swingline (preferred by cautious FMs)- 14% discount for full prepay + 1.5 months swingline buffer funded by Redwood (reconciled on monthly true-up)- Swingline releases in two tranches tied to onboarding milestones- Monthly true-up, amortized credit schedule included in the workbook

Option C — 2yr step-up commitment (best effective rate for multi-year)- Year 1: 16% discount; Year 2: 12% discount (step-down reflects consumption risk)- Quarterly true-up with a mid-year true-up checkpoint and True-Up Cap (20% downward adjustment protection in year 2)- Optional early-termination fee or assignable credit if company consolidates usage to other platforms

Attachments included: Redwood_Annual_Prefund_Options_v1.pdf, RDW-Terms-StepUp-v2.xlsx (term worksheet with amortization examples).

Short notes on mechanics:
- Prefunding/swingline is structured as an escrow-like buffer; funds are reconciled monthly with any overage credited against future invoices.
- Amortized credits are pro-rated monthly and only applied after reconciliation against actual tokens.
- We can do either monthly or quarterly true-up; monthly reduces risk for you but increases ops churn on our side.

If you want, we can propose a blended Option B/C where year 1 has a prefund swingline and year 2 moves to a step-down discount with a quarterly true-up. I'm happy to hop on a short call with your finance and procurement to walk the worksheet.

Adding a few guardrails from a pricing/ops perspective — quick suggestions based on similar deals:

- Hybrid credit ramp: Redwood funds 1.5 months swingline up front for onboarding; Ava funds the remainder of year 1 prepay after a 30-day ramp review. This keeps finance comfortable and reduces Redwood exposure.
- True-up cadence: propose monthly true-ups for months 1–3, then quarterly afterwards (auto-switch) — helpful for new customers with volatile early usage.
- Discount anchoring: anchor to an effective blended discount (e.g., 15% blended across 2 years) instead of strict step-up percentages — simpler for procurement to model.
- Use a per-token floor for the first 90 days to avoid catastrophic overrun risk on prod tests.

If procurement needs it, we can insert a 90-day pilot clause with a reduced commitment that rolls into the annual prepay on automated acceptance (saves procurement from committing blindly).

Happy to join a call next week.

- Ben
